title: What Is Law Part 1
paragraphs: Especially from the perspective of those who grew up within the fold of religion, specifically those who grew up in the Evangelical Protestant faith. This word is very difficult to understand. Actually, I was born in the Bahamas. I was born into a religious family. My father, who is still with us today. I was born and he was a priest. He was a pastor in the Brethren Church when I was first born. Then we moved from the Brethren Church to the Baptist Church. He was also a Baptist minister for most of our lives.

Then my mother moved from the Baptist church and went to the Pentecostal church. And so I got both; I was a " Baptist-Pentecostal". She would take us to the Pentecostal church, and then he would take us to the Baptist church, and that's how my mixed religious culture was formed. We've been through all those experiences, and one of the things they never talked about in any of those churches was "the law". the law. However, the Bible is a book of law.

They kept talking about grace, grace, and freedom, and I suppose that's normal. But I believe that we have been robbed, in a very real sense, of the beauty of the balance between law and grace. I think the result of our experience was that we ended up hating the law. We have learned to love grace and hate the law. I think I understand what they were trying to do because all of us, perhaps in some way, have been strongly affected by the harshness of " legal legitimacy". So I want to talk about that today.

Please get a copy of this series, this session in particular, and listen to it. I'm going to say some things that you haven't heard and won't hear until you hear them for the third time. What is the law? When we use the term law, what are we talking about? We want to understand what I call the "principle of law". What is the true nature of law when we use this term?

Today I need to provide some definitions to ensure that you are not confused, and also to enable you to intelligently share with others what we are trying to understand here today. I would like to begin with a simple statement. Why do we abide by the law? Write this down. Why do we abide by the law? There are religious people who will ask you among those who attend this church: "Does your pastor teach about the Law? Does he take you back to the Law? Does he take you back to slavery?"

But when the Lord first spoke to me about this subject, I had the same questions for Him. I said, "Lord, you want to take me to the Law." And of course, he had to purify me a little and correct my concepts. And he did. He corrected me. So, I want to ask a few questions to clear your minds. Here is the first question. Do we pay taxes and customs duties to become citizens? What is the answer? Are you sure? Okay, I want you to... this is important. Do we pay taxes to become citizens of a country?

Do you pay taxes to become citizens of a country? That's an important question. Taxes, imposing taxes is the law. Paying duties on products you import is the law. So, will you abide by this law to become a citizen? That is the question. The answer is of course no. The second question is, do we stop at the red light to become citizens of a country? no. So, you obey the red light signal. You obey that law. The law states that every time the red light comes on, you must stop your vehicle. Now, this is the law.

It is against the law to drive your car through a red light. So every time you stop at a red light, you are obeying a law. The question is: Is stopping at a red light required to become a citizen? What is the answer? no. The third question is, should we not steal in order to become citizens? no. Should we not kill people in order to become citizens? In other words, as long as I don't kill people, I am a citizen. no. Now, it is against the law to take someone's life.

It is against the law to take people's property without permission. This is the law. But do we do those things in order to become citizens of the country? The answer is no. However, we uphold the laws. The third question is, do we abide by the law in order to become citizens? This is the crux of the matter. Do we have to abide by the law to become citizens? What is the answer? no. Good. So, we have settled this matter. You do not use the law to become a citizen of a country.

You do not abide by the laws to become a citizen of a country. So the law does not make you a citizen of a country. In other words, obeying the laws does not make you a citizen. This is extremely important because I believe this is the point of contention regarding the subject of the law. So, do we abide by the law to become citizens? Absolutely not. But write this down. We abide by the law because we are citizens. This is what is missing in the Kingdom of God society.

When you become a citizen, the law becomes a requirement. You do not abide by the law to become a citizen. You abide by the law because you are a citizen. So what does that mean? This means that this law is not a ritual. When you stop at a red light, that's not weather, is it? no. This is the law. In this session, and hopefully for the rest of your lives, I want to clarify the difference between ritual law and divine law. They are different.

What we struggle with in the body of Christ is the confusion between ritual law and divine law. Can I phrase it like this? We are afraid of the law because we have been taught that the law is slavery. Okay, stop at a red light. Is this slavery? Welcome. Is it slavery? No, but what is it? protection. You are bound by the law to protect your life. Sometimes you are in a hurry and don't want to stop, but you do stop. Why? Because you prefer to reach your destination rather than go to heaven quickly.

So, even though you might want to break that law, you are subject to it because the law is there to protect you. Now make a note of this. The subject of the law is a source of fear for many people. It causes them discomfort, especially when you talk to a Protestant Christian. We do not worship the law. We obey the law. The law exists to serve us. We are not here to serve the law. The subject of law is also a source of conflict for many people.

They say, "Well, you know, I'm saved by grace, so I'm no longer under the law." Well, they quote that from the Bible without understanding, firstly, who the writer was, where he came from, what his history was, and what he was dealing with two thousand years ago in his society with religious people.

This is one of the problems that I believe we have sown in this contemporary church since we have strayed from understanding the origin of the concept of law, to the point that we have become afraid even of thinking about being subject to the law. This leads me to point number three. The subject of law is a source of paranoia (suspiciousness). People become suspicious. Oh, do you mean we have to go back and slaughter the lambs again? Do we need to go back and offer blood again? Those are not divine laws.

Offering a lamb on an altar was a ritual law, not a divine law. I am not suspicious. Can I phrase it this way? My success in life is due to my adherence to God's law. The only way to prove that you are a citizen of a country is by obeying the law. You do not have to abide by the law to become a citizen. You are bound by the law to prove that you are a citizen of that country. In our session last year, oh, God led us through something I had to back away from a little.

Well, you didn't even know that, but you do know that we're talking about the Kingdom Society. You cannot build a kingdom society unless people agree to obey the same laws, because society is a product of laws. So God says: "Step back and return to the law first." What makes the Bahamas, Jamaica, or America a country is the law. That's why the first thing you establish to start a country is a constitution. A constitution is a contract that people make with themselves to abide by certain laws and principles.

This is what makes a country. Now, if you disobey those agreed- upon laws, you are no longer worthy of remaining in society. What are they doing? They take you out of one society and put you in another. It's called prison. If you are rehabilitated, which means you agree to abide by the laws again, they may reintegrate you into the larger community once more. Okay, you can abide by the law.

So we are suspicious because we have been taught that the law is bad, when in fact the law is the best thing that has ever happened to us. In fact, all the bad things that have been happening to you are because of your violation of the law. For example, just the law of good healthy eating. Your arteries are blocked. This is not a demon. These are fats. Where did it come from? It did not come from the devil. Those are pork chops for 20 years, man. And you violated the law of the body. Is my voice being heard?

Then we ask God to heal us. And after he recovers, we go straight back to the filth. It is, as you know, praise be to God. I will celebrate in the filth. You filth, please forgive me. But you know that we think the law is bad. Well, it depends. Yes, write this down. The subject of law is a paradox. People say, " Well, I'm either under the law or under grace." Well, that depends on what they mean by the law, which is something we hope to deal with before we leave.

Because when you use the word law, again, stop using it loosely because there are two kinds of laws. In fact, even three. So when you use the word law, you must be careful because there are three different kinds of laws that we are supposed to live by. One of them is not always the case, and that is what we hope to talk about in this session. Now, why are people afraid of the law? And that's the big word. Write this word. They say they are afraid of legalism. Let everyone speak of legalistic tendencies.

There are many lawyers here today. I have already seen some of them. Lawyers will tell you that the word " legalism" is not a bad word. But religious people, those who claim to have been saved by grace, hate this word. They were actually taught that this word is satanic. Legalistic tendencies. They associate legalism with cults, slavery, oppression, and control. Well, I'm sure that in some cases they have gone through, or seen others go through, certain things that might carry this kind of connotation.

But this term "legalism" is not what you think. What is legalism? I thought I would try to clarify the matter for you. First and foremost, I want to clarify this matter. Civil law is not a ritual. Write that down. Let everyone say "civilian". Say it again. civilian. Now, where does the word "civilian" come from? Civilian. Civilian. What does the term "civil" come from? He comes from a citizen. civilized. People living together in a civilized and organized manner. Being civilized means that we are creatures of law.

When you are uncivilized, what we usually suggest is that you are a savage. You have no control, no self-discipline, no limits. You, you're a monster. You are saying that the girls are behaving in an uncivilized manner. What we mean is that you are acting without control. Okay, what's controlling you? the law.

So when the government of the Bahamas, or the government of Jamaica, or the government of Canada, or the government of the United States uses the word civil law that all countries use, what they mean is that we have made laws so that we can all be civilized. The law brings control, but it's control for your own good. Grace has become a license for uncivilized behavior. But I will sin now because God will forgive me tonight when I pray. You see, we are using grace. This is the aspect of forgiveness.

So that we can be wrong. We do not want limits against sin. Leave me alone. Let me repent after I'm done. God says, "No, you are civilized. You are in my country. You are in my kingdom. You cannot live like this. There are limits in my country. Civil law is not a ritual. Let me explain what I mean by that. The law is designed to bring order. Here is something I will always repeat until I die. God designed everything in life to work according to laws. Why? Laws maintain order.

The law is the most beautiful thing I have discovered. I am not talking about rituals. I am talking about the laws that give life and protect it. Like the law of gravity. What a beautiful law it is. Gravity allows you to stand without falling. Gravity allows this building to stay attached to the ground. Gravity is a powerful law, but we must obey it. You can try to defy gravity very easily. Go up to the top of this building and jump. Say to gravity, 'I rebuke you in the name of Jesus.'

Jesus Christ says, ' Gravity, do your job, dear.'" Boom, I'm dead. Because it's the law. Even if you try to resist it, it works. And gravity is a blessing. Fire is the law of combustion. Fire is the law. You cook with fire, but fire can also burn down your house if you play with matches. So laws are there to cook for you or to cook you. It depends on how you use the law. Is everyone with me? Yes. You can have sex. That's the law. You can have sex within marriage, or outside of marriage.

You can do it any way you want. One will cook for you, and the other will cook you. It's that simple. Your guilt will stay with you forever. God made everything work by law. And wherever there's chaos, you can be sure there's an absence of law or a violation of it. Every accident in the Bahamas you see, every car you see getting into an accident, maybe you see cars piled up somewhere, someone broke the law. We're having this chaos, someone broke the law. You run a red light and now three people are dead.

One person broke the law, and three died. That's chaos. Mark my words. Chaos always precedes destruction. Do you want your life to fall apart? No problem. It's very simple. Just break the laws of life. I'm not talking about religious ritual laws. I'm just talking about the simple laws of life. I repeat, the key to order is the law. When you obey the law, you automatically put your life in order. My life is ordered because of the law.

You know, when the Bible uses the phrase, "The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom," the verse before it says that the law of the Lord is wise. If you fear God's law, you have gained wisdom. What makes me look smart is simply that I learn the laws. People think I'm smart. The Bible says that if a young person learns God's laws, they become wiser than their teachers. How can you become wiser than your teachers? Learn the laws. Because teachers don't know the power of the law. Mark my words.

So, the key to success in life is to obey the law. You don't have to wonder whether you will fail or succeed. And I know, listen, ladies and gentlemen, listen carefully. I know that sometimes your patience runs out. You know, you become impatient because you're waiting for things to happen in your lives. And you say, "Oh Lord, why does it take so long?" "You know what? When you obey God's laws, they start to work. But sometimes it takes time for them to manifest. Keep believing, man. You can have that house.

When you plant a seed in the ground, does it sprout in the morning? But guess what? It's working. You might not see it for weeks, but it's working. Sometimes it stays buried for months. It's working. And one day you see that little thing break through the soil, and you think it's just starting to grow. When you obey God, things start working right away. You know, when September comes, some of you will see the sprouts. And by December, no one will know you're the same person. Why?

Some of the things you obey God in now will show results in November. All you have to do is make sure I obey God's laws. That's all there is to it, obey them and they will work. And they don't work according to what you want. They work according to God's great plans. Like that seed, submit to the laws, and you will prosper. Disobeying the law creates chaos. Life is too simple to make it complicated.

If you're having financial challenges, just look a little deeper into your life and see Whether there's any aspect where you might be breaking some basic rules, like misusing money, not saving properly, or spending on things you probably couldn't afford at the time. Just check; there might be some things you need to review, and... you know, you don't have to blame the devil all the time. Yes. You're asking God to heal you. And God says, " Okay, no problem." Stop eating guava candy ( Dov).

"So you say, 'I bind you in Jesus' name.' And Jesus says, 'I am Jesus.' Stop eating the guava. In other words, we want God to tell us what to do, but we don't want Him to touch what we want to do. Don't touch what we want to do. We, believe me, I love guava, but that sauce is 99% sugar, no, 100%, it's 100% sugar. And when you add butter to it, Lord, I'd better stop talking about it.

I can already see the guilt on your faces, and they say white sugar turns into carbohydrates, is stored in cells as fat, then accumulates in the arteries, and too much ' dove' will kill you. But we say, 'God, please don't touch my dove.' It's a law. So we break the law, and then our bodies are in turmoil. The Bible says, ' Husbands, love your wives.' That's a law. It's a law. Love your wife. It doesn't say the wife should love her husband. Husband, love your wife. Now, love Action.

It's a word that describes an action, which means you can't just say, " I love you." No, no, no, no. You have to do something to prove it. Hey, kid, are you happy to be here? In other words, you can't just say to a woman, "You can assume I love you, baby." Love is an action. You know, I kissed my wife this morning. When I kiss my wife, I miss her. You know, 14 days, kid. Now, I have to say to her, "I kiss you in my mind. I already kissed you in my mind this morning, girl. I don't need to kiss you physically.

You know I love you in my thoughts. You're always on my mind." She'll say, "No, I want you in my life, not in my mind." It's a law. So you wonder when your marriage starts to cool down and tensions and frustrations arise. Why? Because you're breaking a law. Marriage is hard work. Don't rush it, buddy. Don't rush it. You think you're working hard. Get married. I'll be better. It's hard work. And you know what? It's a 24-hour job. Bradley, take it easy, boss.

It's hard work because people think, " Oh, well, hallelujah." "I ca n't enjoy my partner for just three or four hours a day." Oh, really? All day. And you know what? You can't escape it. They go home with you or wait for you at home. It's the law. So when problems start in your marriage, just check if you're following these laws. This isn't a ritual. You know, and your partner knows, when a kiss is just a ritual. They don't want rituals. No rituals. They want the real thing.

Both begin with the letter R in English: ritual or real. You know the difference between ritual and real. Okay. Yeah. Okay. For me, the law takes precedence. Let me make a note of this. Write this down. God's purpose and passion for all of us and all of His creation is to bring His country to Earth. Heaven. Heaven is a country. And the Kingdom is a country, not a religion. I think what we've done is reduce God's program to a religion, which produces rituals, and that's why we hate the law.

What I'm doing in this series is taking the law out of religion, which is ritual, and back to the Kingdom, which is a country. You can't live in the Bahamas without following the laws, or Jamaica, or Barbados, Saint Lucia, America, Canada, Germany, or Haiti. You cannot live in a country without obeying the law. That is the nature of nations. Therefore, if the Kingdom of God is a nation, then nations are built on law. This means that in order to live in the Kingdom of God, we must also be subject to the laws.

We do not use grace to exempt ourselves from obeying the laws. One of the greatest things I have discovered is that life is simple. The law is the key to a successful life. If you know the law of the land and obey it, you will never go to prison. If you stop at a red light, you will never have to look in your rearview mirror for a police officer. In other words, if you obey the law, peace will reign in your mind, and you will not feel guilt in your heart. The law gives you peace.

If you know that you are not committing adultery, you can sleep peacefully with your spouse. If you know that you are not engaging in fornication, you can sleep soundly even on a pole. But the problem, gentlemen, is that if you break the law, the bed becomes as hard as rock. You all know what I am talking about. Some of you, my friend, toss and turn without sleep. The Holy Spirit is at work. Inside you. Why? Because you broke the law. The law brings peace. You know, when I give my tithe, I feel peace. I mean it.

When I make my donations, I tell my wife, I tell her, "My dear, we are giving for the future." "Tithing is for the present. Donations are for the future. You shouldn't be satisfied with just tithes. Tithes support the household, but donations are an investment for the future." It's the law. That is why the Bible says: " Bring your tithes and your offerings." They are both different. You never double the tithe. God does not double the tithes He returns to you because they are a tax. You are not doubling your taxes.

You are doubling down on investments. This is the law. It might be a good idea, while I know now, if the Lord speaks to you, to come and put an offering here in this place. I'm serious. Perhaps the Lord said, "My son, you know, this is true." Try an investment this morning because by October, you may need it to come back to you. The Bible says: “Cast your bread upon the waters today, and it will return to you after many days.” In other words, if you're not going to throw anything, don't go to the beach, you know.

So, what do you do on the beach? Are you waiting for a ship to arrive? But you didn't send anything at all. "Cast your bread upon the waters," he says, " and it will come back to you after many days." So don't go to the beach if you haven't put bread in the water. Law is the key to life. Now let me give you the main points I would like to raise today. There are two main types of laws. Three, but I'll take two now for clarity. First, there are the ritual laws. Write this down. Ritual laws. What are the ritual laws?

Ritual laws are temporary secondary rituals, customs, systems, and programs required for corrective and redemptive purposes. It's a long sentence, but it's necessary. Every word in it is important. What is liturgical law? Say it with me. What is liturgical law? Secondary law, temporary law, ritual law, customary law. What systems and software are required for what purpose? Corrective and redemptive purposes. This means that ritual laws are necessary because something has gone wrong. It's not permanent.

Give an example. You go to the hospital and your lungs stop working. Now, did you know that your lungs operate according to an automatic law? You never try to breathe. Are you thinking about it? You have been breathing for the past two hours and it has not been part of your consciousness, because in your body there is a natural system built in where your lungs rise and fall, you inhale and you exhale, inhaling and exhaling. It's the law. God has placed this law in your body.

Now you go to the hospital and your lungs stop working. We call it a collapse. What are they doing? They connect you to a device. Am I right? They call it a mechanical lung. It does what your lungs have stopped doing. It's weather. What is it? It's secondary. It's not your real lung. It's temporary. You won't stay there all the time. It's just a ritual. They connect you to it. They actually have to do it. It is customary for them to do this if you lose your ability to breathe. It is also a system.

It's also a program. They program it to keep working until your lungs recover. Now that you regain your ability to breathe, what happens? It has been corrected. Once it's corrected, you're freed from that electronic lung. So what are you? free. But you are not free to breathe. You are free to continue breathing. But this time you return to the law that God has placed in your body. Glory to God. In other words, rituals are always temporary. What the church should not deal with or submit to is liturgical law.

This is what the Bible says we should stop doing. We no longer need artificial lungs. Jesus Christ has restored us to our natural state, but we still have to breathe. You are not free to breathe. You are free from relying on rituals to breathe. So this is the first type of law that I want you to understand. The second type of law is called the principles of the law of creation. I wrote this in this way so that it would be clear to you. This is the most important law in life. Principles of the Law of Creation.

In other words, laws are built into us. Let me read it with you. What is the principle of the law of creation? What is it? These are natural principles and standards inherent in creation, necessary and essential for effective functioning. This is the law of creation established by the Creator. These are the laws that you and I are supposed to obey in the kingdom of God. It was a ritual for a high priest to take a lamb into the Holy of Holies. That did not exist at creation. Burning incense was a ritual.

He represented the presence of God. You do not need incense if God is present. I'm going to get into trouble now, but I'm going to take the risk. You don't need the oil anymore, even though we use it. Because the oil was a ritual representing the Holy Spirit, which was absent from man. That's why the priest used oil. But when the spirit returns, you don't need the oil. But as you can see, we are confused. We take the oil and when you use it, oh, I'm going to get into trouble. I can feel it.

You religious people are still here. When you put oil on a person, you are telling the Holy Spirit: I am not entirely sure that you are enough. Wearing dresses, for example. God was specific. The priest told him to wear linen. Do not let it touch your skin. He says: "Wear clothes that allow air to circulate." He says, "Don't make it too tight." Let it be loose. "Why? Because it represents righteousness and holiness. It is beautiful. He said, 'Put all kinds of beautiful things on it.'" Why?

Now, we don't need that anymore. He says: "I have clothed you with righteousness through Jesus Christ." " Oh, now look at this. I'm in trouble. I'm in trouble. So when you see someone wearing a robe, he's saying to God: Your work hasn't been enough yet. It's a different kind of law. He said He freed you from the law. This is what freed you from it. No more lambs and doves and turtledoves and taking incense and wearing all these strange clothes. He said: ' Look, you don't need that anymore.'"

That's why, when Christ came, He never wore a uniform. There is no command in Jesus' name to wear a garment. There is no such thing in the New Testament. He never told us to build a building. He told Moses to build a building. Why? Because the house he used to live in had decayed. Your body cast it out into the garden. Chapter 3, we got rid of the inhabitant. So God said, " Look, since your house is completely decayed, I will build a house for you to live in temporarily." I will call it the meeting tent.

And now, in two thousand years, I will work on it. In four thousand years, I will reclaim my home. I will cleanse it with my blood. Then Christ came and said: I will receive the Holy Spirit. He returned home. You no longer need to build a church with strange decorations. He has returned to his original home. But I cannot teach these things. When we first built this building, do you know what the priests told me? This is not a church. They said, "How dare you call it the Diplomatic Center? That's not a sacred name."

They said, "Man, I've received so many letters." They said, "There is no tower on top of this building. There is no cross in the building. What are you doing? There are no wooden benches. We were the first to use chairs. Ah," they say, "my God, wooden benches make the place sacred." "There is no platform for singing." I mean, they were saying, "There is no altar." "There is no table for eating." They say, "Hey, don't you understand?" "This is the law from which you were freed.

Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit. Therefore, keep it clean. They say, you know, some people clean the building but not their own lives. There are many people in churches today who sweep the floor, wipe the windows, and then go live with someone they are not married to. They clean the house they built, not the house he built. Rituals. That's why people love rituals. They can hide behind them. So they come into this building and kneel, you know, and say, ' God, look what I'm doing.'" Look, do you see that?

Look at my situation, my appearance. And God says, “What about your heart? Are you still under the law after that club you went to last night? The law. Two kinds of law. He never freed you from His law. He freed you from the law that you forced Him to give you temporarily because of your sin. Is my point clear today? This is very important. In fact, write this down. Ritual laws are temporary. Ritual laws are always temporary. Jesus Christ freed us from rites, not from divine laws.

You know that one of the laws that God gave, the divine law, is in the Ten Commandments. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not commit fornication. Fornication is having sex outside of marriage. Okay. Now, this is amazing. We say that we are under grace now, and we are not under the law. Do you know what that means now? I can commit fornication and still be covered by grace. Are you free from fornication because you were born again? This is why the young people in our churches are in such a mess.

This is why the older people in our churches are in such a mess, because this whole grace thing has corrupted the whole church. How A young man listening to me today in this church repeatedly asks for forgiveness for something he keeps doing because they refuse to obey God's law. Then we want God to give us benefits in this country. Lord, bless me. Pay my tuition. God said, "Do you know something?" "You're supposed to be in jail." That's what we do to people who break the law. We lock them up, don't we, Terry?

Do you know why we lock them up? Because they're bad for the whole community. These leaders, people like us, God have mercy. You don't want to be one of us. The Bible says the leaders will be beaten more severely than their followers. The pressure is on us because we don't just teach the law, we're supposed to be the embodiment of the law for the people.

That's why I don't understand how people can attend religious services, knowing the pastor is doing wrong things, and still sit in the front row every day saying, "Amen." Amen. Who is this man? Learn that someone should say, "Hey, one minute, you're encouraging lawbreaking." Please write this down. The laws of creation are eternal. The ritual laws are temporary. Do you think fish could evolve to the point where they no longer need water? Can you imagine a group saying, "I'm fed up with the water.

I'm leaving this ocean. I've been here for 5,000 years. I'm ready to leave now." The laws of creation never change. Never change. You cannot go beyond the stage of not stealing. You know, I've been stealing for 50 years, so I can afford to do it now. Look, you don't do that. You, these laws are divine laws. You know, I haven't killed anyone in 20 years, so I could kill someone now. Look, you don't do that. This is a divine law. In the past, we used to offer sheep for our sins every year.

But that was a ritual law because of the correction. It has been corrected through the cross. We no longer need to offer lambs. Oh, but you still must not commit adultery. Why me, Lord? Write this down. Ritual laws. Hebrews, chapter 10. Record them in your notes. Hebrews chapter 10, verse 1 says: “ What is the law?” A shadow of good things to come. The word " Namous" here refers to ritual laws. In the Old Testament, after Adam sinned, God called Noah. Then Abraham called out.
